summary.text: Chris Banks represents the 42nd District on the New York City Council, which includes East New York, Starrett City, Brownsville, Canarsie, Remsen Village and East Flatbush in Brooklyn.
His Council biography describes him as a lifelong Brooklyn resident and community and tenant organizer.

paragraphs.text: Banks was born and raised in East New York, the son of an immigrant mother from Trinidad and Tobago and a father from Houston, Texas, according to his Council biography.
He attended PS 213, PS 273 and Anointed Minds Christian Academy, graduated from Leadership Public Service High School in Manhattan, and attended John Jay College of Criminal Justice.

His first job was as an education group leader and adolescent coordinator at the local Police Athletic League, and he later ran after-school and summer youth programs for the East New York Local Development Corporation.

The biography says he founded or co-founded East New York United Concerned Citizens Inc. and the East New York Collaborative, served as president of the 75th Precinct Council and the Van Siclen Block Association, and was a member of Community Board 5.
It credits his organizing with preventing a rent increase at Starrett City and the closure of two senior centers.
